title: Fault family — ProofRequirementKind.IntervalContainment: an assigned/computed numeric value's interval must fit the target field's (or element band's) declared bounds

citations.note: Fault family: the catalog-declared safety precondition at the evaluation site; premise classes (b)/(c)/(a) per catalog ProofSatisfactions, with (a)/(d) admitted for the fault family under the 2026-07-21 citation duty
Fault minting: each evaluation site in a plan mints its own fault obligations; site identity is an occasion, not a syntactic position

2026-07-21 citation-duty ruling (class (a)/(d) admitted for the fault family only under a named establishing + preserving obligation set, each discharged) and the open design hole that nothing detects an unminted obligation
Ratification gate: no cell ratifies whose derivation cites an argument-less rule
The seven named validity arguments; 'Arg-bound interval arithmetic' (with its guard-spelled variant) and 'Literal constant-fold for defaults' are the two this family's defined cells rest on

IntervalContainmentProofRequirement — the DU subtype: Subject, TargetField, DeclaredMin/Max, AuthoredMin/Max. hasCatalogSite is false — no operator/function/action carries an IntervalContainment slot in its ProofRequirements; the instance is engine-synthesized from declared bounds
ProofRequirementMeta.IntervalContainment -> DiagnosticCode.NumericOverflow (PRE0078) — the diagnostic every rejection in this family carries

IntervalOfNarrowed — the single interval computation all three mint sites discharge through: literal -> point; TypedArgRef -> ExtractArgInterval (class b); TypedFieldRef -> ExtractFieldInterval (class a); guard narrowing via the narrowed dict (class c, field reads only)

the transport dependency the discharges rest on: ingress-governed argument facts are earned at phase 1 and never killed (nothing in a plan writes an argument); guard facts are killed by an intervening write to deps — the frame-and-kill rule the matrix's 2026-07-21 soundness correction depends on, restated in docs/Working/transport-rule-restatement-2026-07-21.md § What earns a fact

notes: Interval-containment band members are algebraic rearrangements of a bound that the interval arithmetic does not cover — e.g. a bound spelled as `interval(RHS) <= declaredMax - Offset` (a term moved across the inequality) is sound but no interval derivation follows the move. Its respelling is the direct bound (`RHS + Offset` bounded, or a per-term guard/arg bound) — the same respelling shape as Witness Family 1. cells.premiseAvailability: The RHS reads the triggering event's own argument directly, with no intervening computation (spec:164, :170 purity), so premise (b) is available: governance enforces the arg's declared bound at ingress before the write reads it (spec:268; transport § What earns a fact — an ingress-governed argument fact is earned at phase 1 and never killed). ExtractArgInterval (ProofEngine.Intervals.cs:312) turns the arg's declared min/max into the operand interval the containment test consumes. Premise (c) via a guard bounding the arg is provable under the model (the 'Arg-bound interval arithmetic' guard-spelled variant), but is NOT offered as a built discharge arm here: BuildNarrowedIntervals (ProofEngine.Intervals.cs:519) narrows FIELD reads only — IntervalOfNarrowed's TypedArgRef case (:99) ignores the narrowing dict — so a guard on the arg does not tighten its interval in the shipped engine. Premise (a) (field modifiers on the RHS) is not exercised: the RHS is an arg, not a field, so no field sits in the read position. Premise (d) is not part of this cell's contract for the same reason recorded across the division fault group: the matrix names no validity argument for a rule-premised (CompositionalConstraint) discharge of a fault obligation, and the citation-duty machinery it would require does not exist (matrix § Rule validity gate; § The cell open design hole).

dischargeContract.derivation: governance enforces the event arg's declared bound before the write reads it; ExtractArgInterval yields [argMin .. argMax]; containment holds iff that interval ⊆ [declaredMin .. declaredMax] -> IntervalContainment strategy
dischargeContract.decisionProcedure: Compute the RHS interval from the arg's declared bounds (ExtractArgInterval, a finite read of declared modifiers). Accept iff [argMin .. argMax] ⊆ [declaredMin .. declaredMax] (subset test); an arg interval whose lower is below declaredMin or whose upper exceeds declaredMax, or an unbounded operand, rejects with NumericOverflow (PRE0078).

cells.premiseAvailability: The introduced element reads the event's own arg, so premise (b) is available exactly as in the scalar cell (ingress governance + ExtractArgInterval). Premise (a)/(c)/(d) excluded for the same reasons. One built-behavior nuance recorded, not a definition claim: the element band folds nonnegative/positive into a real lower bound (GetElementNumericBounds, ProofEngine.Intervals.cs:279), whereas ExtractArgInterval does NOT fold the arg's nonnegative flag — so a `nonnegative max N` arg gives [−∞ .. N], which fails an element band [0 .. N] on the lower bound. To discharge, the arg needs an explicit `min` (a DeclarationValue lower bound) or the element band must omit the lower bound. This is a built-engine asymmetry, not part of the discharge contract, and is why the witness uses a `max N` element band (band [−∞ .. N]) so the arg's [−∞ .. N] is contained.

cells.premiseAvailability: A state entry/exit action runs on any transition into/out of its anchor state and is NOT bound to a specific event, so its RHS cannot read event args — premise (b) is structurally unavailable here (confirmed against samples: `to Investigation -> set InvestigatedAt = now()`, `to ReadyToReturn -> set ShippingLabelSent = true` — hooks read fields/literals). The available discharge is premise (c): the hook's own `when` guard narrows a read field. BuildNarrowedIntervals reads the state hook's guard (StateHookContext -> s.Hook.Guard, ProofEngine.Intervals.cs:526) and IntervalOfNarrowed applies the narrowed interval to the TypedFieldRef (:67-69). The guard fact is earned at the hook's guard evaluation (phase 6, entry) and reaches the hook's own action with no intervening write to the read field (transport § What earns a fact / § The transport rule — frame-and-kill: deps(φ) ∩ mayWrite between guard and action is empty). Premise (a) (reading the field's OWN declared bound as the operand interval, via ExtractFieldInterval) is a real built mechanism but is EXCLUDED from the contract: the matrix admits class (a) for the fault family only under the 2026-07-21 citation duty (name the establishing + every preserving obligation, each discharged), no such machinery exists, and no named validity argument covers a field-modifier interval read of a fault obligation — recorded as a missing rule (openFlag), not resolved here.

dischargeContract.derivation: the hook's `when` guard supplies a per-term bound on the read field; BuildNarrowedIntervals narrows that field's interval; containment holds iff the narrowed interval ⊆ the declared band -> IntervalContainment (guard-spelled variant of arg-bound interval arithmetic)
dischargeContract.decisionProcedure: Extract the hook guard's per-term bound conjuncts over the read field (a finite set), narrow the field's interval, and accept iff the narrowed RHS interval ⊆ [declaredMin .. declaredMax]; a guard that does not bound the field on the failing side, or none, rejects with NumericOverflow (PRE0078). Sound only if no construct on the route between the guard and the action writes the read field (transport frame-and-kill) — satisfied here (entry-hook guard and action are adjacent at phase 6).

citations.note: Arg-bound interval arithmetic — 'the same argument carries the guard-spelled variant — the per-term bound conjuncts the band ruling licenses'; inherits the 2026-07-21 no-intervening-write soundness correction

cells.premiseAvailability: A computed field expression reads other FIELDS only — it has no event-arg scope and no `when` guard — so neither premise (b) (arg bounds) nor premise (c) (guard narrowing) is available. The sole discharge path is premise (a): reading each input field's OWN declared bound as an operand interval (ExtractFieldInterval, ProofEngine.Intervals.cs:202) and combining via the operators' IntervalTransfer functions. The built engine DOES perform this (live-verified: `field Sum as integer max 100 <- A + B` with A,B `nonnegative max 50` proves, computed interval [0 .. 100]; with A,B unbounded it rejects, PRE0078). BUT under the matrix this class-(a) discharge of a fault obligation is licensed only under the 2026-07-21 citation duty (name the establishing and every preserving obligation of each input field's bound, each discharged) — and (1) that machinery does not exist (no establishment/preservation ProofRequirement subtype, matrix § Obligation family), and (2) no named validity argument covers a field-modifier interval read for a fault obligation ('Arg-bound interval arithmetic' is grounded in ingress governance of event args, not in a field's declared bound being true of its runtime value across writes). Per the ratification gate, this cell CANNOT record a discharge contract without citing an argument-less rule. Left OPEN — a missing rule for the owner.

base.program:
precept W

field A as integer default 0
field B as integer default 0
field Sum as integer max 100 <- A + B

state Active initial

event Create() initial
event SetInputs(AVal as integer, BVal as integer)

on Create
    -> set A = 0

from Active on SetInputs
    -> set A = SetInputs.AVal
    -> set B = SetInputs.BVal
    -> no transition

cells.premiseAvailability: Same structure as the primitive computed cell — only class (a) (input field bounds) is available, with no validity argument. Additionally recorded: even the built engine cannot discharge the money case today. Live-verified: `field Total as money in 'USD' max '1000 USD' <- PartA + PartB` with PartA, PartB `nonnegative max '500 USD'` yields a computed interval of [−∞ .. +∞] (money field reads / money `+` return an unbounded interval — the IntervalTransfer / ExtractFieldInterval money path is not built), so Total stays Unresolved and rejects with PRE0078 regardless of the operand bounds. Contrast the primitive `Rate * Hours` and `A + B` cases, which DO compute a finite interval. So this cell is BOTH model-open (no validity argument for class a) AND built-unresolved (money operand intervals unbuilt).
